node_definition.done_when: Read section 29 of crew-observability-truth first. First reproduce the defect at your base: find each outcome path of crew dispatch (crew_dispatch in reckon/cli.py, and what it calls in reckon/crew/dispatch.py, which you may read but not write) that writes more than one document or any non-JSON text to stdout, and name each path with its line in the manifest. If no path does so at your base, write status blocked naming each path you checked, rather than adding a test that cannot fail. Then every crew dispatch outcome, whether launched, refused, dry run or error, writes exactly one JSON document to stdout, and every additional notice goes to stderr. Make that structural in reckon/cli.py: everything crew_dispatch calls runs with stdout redirected to stderr, and only the final emission writes to stdout. That holds for a notice printed anywhere beneath, including code this node cannot edit. tests/test_dispatch_stdout_is_one_document.py drives each path that emitted an extra through click's CliRunner with stdout and stderr captured separately, and asserts that json.loads(stdout) parses. At least one case fails at your base. Existing tests reaching crew_dispatch output keep passing; grep tests/ for crew_dispatch, CLI invocations of crew dispatch and _emit to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/dispatch-stdout-is-one-document.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
